subject: general
question: In one hour, a boat goes 46 km/hr in the direction of the stream and 36 km/hr against the direction of the stream. What will be the speed of the current?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed of Stream** = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream = (46 − 36) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef652caf007788903eb53e9509a5fdf7ae772c3ae3dc1990f73f0738f935bbf0.png] 

**Given:**

Downstream Speed (D) = 46 km/hr

Upstream Speed (U) = 36 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Let speed of boat in **still water** be 'u' and speed of **current** be 'v'.

D = u + v

U = u − v

Speed of current (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ v = (46 − 36) ÷ 2

⇒ v = 10 ÷ 2

⇒ v = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: u = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2.

Downstream vs Upstream

Downstream speed is always greater than upstream speed because the **current** assists the boat.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream; Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream.</p
